en.title: Obergurgl snow forecast next week (23–29 November 2026): a minor top-up of 13 cm
en.description: Obergurgl will get 13 cm at the top next week (23–29 Nov), with the best day on 26 Nov. Light refresh, not a storm.
en.lede: Next week at Obergurgl is a gentle snow week, not a powder event. The forecast shows 13 cm at the top (ranging 3 to 23 cm) and 11 cm at the base from Monday 23 to Sunday 29 November, so this is a modest refresh of the existing snow rather than the kind of dump that changes your plans.

sections.h: Where the snow falls across the mountain
p: Obergurgl spreads its next-week snow fairly evenly from base to summit. Upper slopes (around 3000 m) are forecast at 13 cm, the middle of the mountain at 12 cm, and the base at 11 cm. That narrow spread means the snow line stays well below the village, so you will ski in fresh snow all the way down.

The range of uncertainty widens at each height—the top could see as little as 3 cm or as much as 23 cm—but the pattern is consistent: a system that is not fussy about altitude. This matters if you are thinking about where the snow will stick longest; it will not favour the highest slopes dramatically over the mid-mountain terrain.

sections.h: When to be on the mountain
p: The 13 cm is not handed out evenly across seven days. Thursday 26 November is the standout day, with 6 cm forecast at the top and up to 10 cm in the best-case range. Wednesday 25 brings 2 cm (up to 4), and Friday 27 adds another 1–2 cm. The rest of the week is nearly dry.

If you are chasing the softest turns, Thursday 26 is your window. It is enough to soften the pistes, though not enough to call it a powder day. The Hohe Mut and Wurmkogel above Hochgurgl hold snow longest and deserve priority on that day.

sections.h: How next week compares with this week
p: Before next week arrives, Obergurgl will have already received 8 cm at the top from 17 to 20 November (ranging 5 to 10 cm). That is a thinner layer, so next week's snow lands on a modest base. The two weeks together—8 cm now, 13 cm later—build a firmer snowpack than either week alone, but neither week is a game-changer on its own.

This is the rhythm of early-season Obergurgl. The resort is famous for snow that lasts because of its height and cold, not because it gets hammered by single storms. Many small tops add up to the season's story.

The storm is regional, not local. Sölden (10 km away) gets 13 cm at the top next week, Stubai Glacier (14 km away) gets 14 cm, and Hintertux (52 km away) also gets 14 cm. Obergurgl sits at 13 cm, so it is in the middle of the pack, not an outlier.

A few centimetres difference at this scale is well within forecast uncertainty. The same system is moving through, so your choice of resort should rest on terrain, aspect and which lifts are running, not on chasing an extra 1 cm of snow.

The gap between the low-end (3 cm) and high-end (23 cm) forecasts is wide for a week ahead. That range tells you the storm's track and strength are still settling. Storm timing tends to lock in first; the actual depth keeps shifting until a day or two before it arrives.
Watch the forecast as Wednesday approaches. A shift of just 100 km would push the system north or south, and the totals would follow. For now, treat 13 cm as a solid mid-range guess, not a guarantee.

sections.h: What to expect at the base
p: The base gets nearly as much snow as the top, so the snow line will stay well below the lowest lifts all week. Fresh snow down to Obergurgl village is the most likely picture. That means travel access should stay good, and the village itself will be white for most of the period.

The main risk is if air temperatures swing mild mid-week. Even at 1784 m, a warm spell can slow accumulation or even trigger melt on south-facing slopes. The regional avalanche bulletin and a check with the resort on the day will tell you what is happening on the ground.

advice: Thursday 26 November is the best day next week; plan your visit around that date if you want the most snow.
Fresh snow on a young snowpack means avalanche risk exists. Consult the regional avalanche service of Tyrol before any off-piste outing.
Early season: ring Obergurgl directly to confirm which lifts are open and running before you travel, especially on the upper peaks.
With only 13 cm and a thin base beneath it, this week is for consolidating the season, not for a dedicated powder hunt.
The snow line is forecast to stay low, so the village should stay white, but watch the mid-week weather forecast for any sudden warmth.
